description: 1. The agent must locate the neuralink-decoder skill package at /workspace/neuralink_decoder_pkg/ and read the SKILL.md to understand the available `decode` command. 2. The agent must install the package (pip install -e /workspace/neuralink_decoder_pkg/) if not already installed, or discover it is already installed via the setup_script. 3. The agent must invoke `neuralink-decoder decode` (the exact CLI command from the SKILL.md) to run the simulation — a naive agent trying to write their own BCI simulator from scratch with arbitrary parameters will produce wrong numerical values. 4. The agent must capture the stdout of the decode command, which prints a formatted table with columns timestep, vx, vy. 5. The agent must parse that output and write a properly-formatted CSV file named `trajectory_data.csv` with header row `timestep,vx,vy` and exactly 100 data rows (derived from T_TOTAL=5.0s / DT=0.05s = 100 timesteps) with the deterministic values from the seed=7 RNG. The proprietary trap: any agent that tries to implement cosine tuning BCI decoding from scratch will produce different numerical values and/or a different number of timesteps, failing the determinism check.
